items.title: Frank Amacker Interview, 1960-09-30
items.q: See, even the Peter Ron, even the Peter Buccott. He was better. See, he had more knowledge of the violin.

ctx.x: Who did Herbert Lindsay play with?

Now, Herbert Lindsay, that was a crackerjack violin player. He was one of the best. Now, you call the man's name there. He was one of the best violinists that I would listen to for this particular reason. Herbert Lindsay could make more, yet, listen, yet he's an air player. But he could make more double stops in a manner I renew in my life. See, from anything he played. And catch it right now, solo, classic, or whatever it was. And make all double, fashion, he could make more double stops. And then he ran out of…
But where did he play Herbert Lindsay? Did he play along?

items.title: Frank Amacker Interview, 1960-07-01
items.q: I used to play with him, I forgot to call his name. I was sitting in bands with him and played.

ctx.x: What about Big Al Louis Robertson, the piano player, not Big Al Louis the clarinet player? Do you know him? Sir Robertson, no, I don't know. What about Cato? Do you know him? Yeah, I know Cato. He's uptown there. Which one? Cato. Cato. Big Cato or Little Cato? Big Cato. He's still living. It's still uptown there,

towards the Irish Channel. I'll try to locate him for you if you want. They'll try to locate him for you. Yeah, if you want to cross him. Yeah. You know? Cato and then there. Old timers, old timers. They were very popular in that day. Very popular. Oh, they were very popular in that day. Oh, they played with jazz in that day like that.
